C009.claim: No CMS/ATLAS analysis targets semi-visible / semi-dark Higgs decays (h->Z(ll)X with X invisible, or non-resonant h->ll+MET / jj+MET from dark-sector EFT operators), so a dedicated HL-LHC search would fill a gap left by H->invisible and H->gamma+gamma_D searches.
C009.surviving_gap: (a) h->Z X(inv) [semi-dark, resonant Z]: no dedicated CMS/ATLAS search found; it is a gap, but the physics room is small. The best published HL-LHC phenomenology study (2206.01214, ZH->4l+MET, NN) reaches BR(h->ZX)xBR(X->inv) ~ 2.8 x BR(h->Z nu nu)_SM ~ 1.5% at 2 sigma. That is only about 2-8x stronger than the indirect bound from HL-LHC H->inv (h->Z(nu nu)X counts as invisible) and from the Higgs-rate global fits. What survives is a dedicated h->Z+MET search that combines the ZH(4l+MET), VBF and boosted ggF categories and is interpreted for ALP/2HDM+a/dark photon X in m_X ~ 1-30 GeV. Its value is modest unless several production modes are combined. (b) Non-resonant h->ll+MET / jj+MET (DSMEFT, 2511.09778): no experimental search found, but the claimed HL-LHC reach is not credible as it stands (see showstoppers). It needs a re-study with the full background set before it can count as an analysis gap.

kill_evidence.what: The HL-LHC Yellow Report (WG2) uses a combined VBF+VH projected limit mu*BR_inv <= 2.5% (Eq. 126). Since BR(Z->nu nu) ~ 20%, h->ZX with X invisible feeds h->inv at ~0.2*BR(h->ZX). That indirectly caps BR(h->ZX) at roughly 12% (my estimate, not in the source). The Higgs-rate global fit (Table 78, values not read: UNVERIFIED) also constrains BR(h->ZX) generically. So the direct search competes with existing HL-LHC projections over only a narrow window.

The HL-LHC phenomenology for the semi-dark mode already exists: ZH, 4l+MET, NN analysis, 2 sigma reach BR x BR = 2.8 x BR(h->Z nu nu)_SM for m_X = 1 GeV at 3 ab^-1 (BR(h->Z nu nu)_SM = 5.4e-3 quoted). C017.claim: CMS/ATLAS HNL searches assume pure Majorana or Dirac limits and/or combine OS+SS dilepton samples. The LNV/LNC (SS/OS) ratio and the time-resolved heavy neutrino-antineutrino oscillation pattern of pseudo-Dirac HNL pairs, which encode the mass splitting, are not exploited.

HL-LHC phenomenology exists (2212.00562, CMS-like Delphes), but no experimental result does this. The window is small: resolvable oscillations need c tau_osc ~ mm-cm and long-lived N (m_N ~ 5-20 GeV, |theta|^2 ~ 1e-7-1e-6). Current ATLAS/CMS displaced HNL limits already reach that region, so the HL-LHC event yield in the surviving window may be too small to resolve oscillations.
